column1: # The law units the ablation asks about, largest first.
# TAB-SEPARATED, SIX COLUMNS: id, key sentence, what it is, where it lives,
# approximate bytes, pinned.
# THE KEY SENTENCE IS A LOCATOR AND NOT A QUOTE OF THE WHOLE LAW. ablate.sh
# finds the blank-line-delimited block it sits in and removes that block, so the
# sentence only has to be unique on the page — but it MUST be verbatim, because
# a sentence that no longer matches makes the script exit rather than silently
# ablate nothing and report a null result.
# `where` decides which road ablate.sh can take. A unit in `system.md` can be
# cut by patching a throwaway worktree. A unit rendered from `beltfacts.go` is a
# Go string chosen by a predicate, and there is no honest way to cut one out of
# a Markdown file — those units need the AFORGE_PROMPT_ABLATE hook lane C or
# lane G may add. Until it exists, they are listed here and cannot be run, which
# is the state of the world and not an omission.
# `pinned` names a law a substring test holds in place (the wave brief's list,
# DESIGN.md §6). A pinned law DOES NOT MOVE ON THIS SCRIPT'S EVIDENCE. It is
# still worth ablating — knowing what a law is worth is useful even when the law
# is staying — but the result is a note in BENCH.md, never a deletion.
# The bytes are DESIGN.md §1's audit figures for the family, not a measurement
# this file made. They order the list; they do not appear in any table.
